topic: Fix a blown-out sky with a layer mask

steps.title: The sky is blown out
steps.narration: Your sky is completely blown out, but the land looks perfect. Here's the thirty second fix the pros actually use.

steps.title: Don't darken the whole photo
steps.narration: If you just pull the exposure down on everything, the sky gets better, but the rocks turn muddy. So we'll darken only the sky.

steps.title: Add an Exposure adjustment layer
steps.narration: At the bottom of the layers panel, click the adjustment icon, and choose Exposure.

steps.title: Drag exposure down
steps.narration: Drag the exposure slider down to about minus one point two. Yes, the whole image gets darker for now. That's fine.

steps.title: Invert the mask
steps.narration: Every adjustment layer comes with a white mask, so the effect shows everywhere. Click the mask, then press Control I to invert it to black. The effect disappears.

steps.title: Paint the sky back in
steps.narration: Now press B for the brush, press D so white is your foreground color, and paint over the sky. Everywhere you paint white, the darker sky comes back.

steps.title: Soften the edge
steps.narration: The edge along the cliffs is a little harsh, so open the mask properties, and drag feather to about forty pixels.

steps.title: Check your mask
steps.narration: Alt click the mask to see exactly what you painted. White is the sky you changed, black is protected. Alt click again to go back.

steps.title: Before and after
steps.narration: And here's the before, and the after. Same photo, but now you can actually see the clouds. Follow for more editing tricks.

youtube.description:
Darken only the sky with an Exposure adjustment layer, an inverted mask and a soft white brush - then feather the edge. Works in Photoshop and most layer-based editors.
